_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who have progressed on or are intolerant to crizotinib; approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, non-comparative, open-label, multicenter trial evaluating two brigatinib dosing regimens; patients randomized 1:1 to Arm A (90 mg once daily) or Arm B (90 mg once daily lead-in → 180 mg once daily).
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC who had progressed on crizotinib.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1; FDA used IRC-assessed confirmed ORR as the major efficacy outcome measure.
pivotal_trials.n: N=222 randomized (Arm A 90 mg n=112; Arm B 90→180 mg n=110).
pivotal_trials.result: In the labeled 90→180 mg arm (N=110): IRC-assessed ORR 53% (95% CI 43-62) with median DOR 13.8 months (95% CI 9.3-NE); investigator-assessed ORR 54% (95% CI 44-63). In the 90 mg arm (N=112): IRC ORR 48% (95% CI 39-58). IRC intracranial ORR in patients with measurable brain metastases was 67% (95% CI 41-87) in the 90→180 mg arm.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥25%) were nausea, diarrhea, fatigue, cough, and headache. Serious risks include ILD/pneumonitis occurring early (within 9 days; median onset 2 days) in 6.4% of patients with Grade 3-4 in 2.7%; hypertension; bradycardia; visual disturbance; CPK elevation.
target_moa: Brigatinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor with in vitro activity against multiple kinases including ALK, ROS1, IGF-1R, FLT-3 and EGFR (deletion/point mutations); highest activity against ALK with an IC50 of 0.6 nM.

rems.type: A REMS is not needed to ensure that the benefits of brigatinib outweigh its risks.

companion_dx_detail: No specific companion diagnostic was approved; eligibility required documented ALK rearrangement confirmed by an FDA-approved test (Vysis ALK Break-Apart FISH Probe Kit was used in the trial). FDA found no issues of concern related to the test.

advisory_committee.vote: The Division did not obtain the advice of the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) for this NDA; it consulted a practicing oncologist and a patient physician who agreed with the favorable risk-benefit assessment.

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to full approval and broadened indication to all adult patients with ALK-positive metastatic NSCLC (removing the prior crizotinib-treated limitation)

citations.quote: The updated indication based on this supplemental application is for the treatment of adult patients with anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) as detected by an FDA-approved test. In addition, the DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION, WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, ADVERSE REACTIONS, USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY, and CLINICAL STUDIES sections of labeling have been revised with the results of the clinical trial verifying the clinical benefit of brigatinib in this population.

description.text: Revised CLINICAL STUDIES section to incorporate additional long-term efficacy data from Study 301 (ALTA 1L), fulfilling the overall survival postmarketing commitment; no new indication added

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for revisions to the CLINICAL STUDIES (14) section of the US Prescribing Information (USPI) for Alunbrig, incorporating additional long-term efficacy data supported by findings from Study 301 (ALTA 1L). This sNDA also provides for revisions to the DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION (2.3, Dosage Modifications for Adverse Reactions), WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS (5.7, Hepatotoxicity), and PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION (17) sections of the USPI.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Tumor response rate (durable objective response rate) and duration of response; a 53% IRC-assessed response rate in the 110 patients receiving the labeled dose.

summary.text: NDA 208772 received a Priority review and was granted accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H based on a durable 53% IRC-assessed response rate and duration of response in the single ALTA trial, with a required confirmatory trial (Study AP26113-13-301) versus crizotinib in the first-line setting. The NDA was treated as an orphan drug (pediatric assessment exemption under 21 CFR 314.55(d)).

The recommendation for accelerated approval according to 21 CFR 314.510 Subpart H is primarily based on the results of a single trial (ALTA) that demonstrated a durable 53% Independent Review Committee-assessed response rate in 110 patients in the study arm where patients received the brigatinib dose proposed in product labeling.

As a condition of accelerated approval, one or more clinical trials will be required to further verify and describe the clinical benefit of brigatinib in patients with metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC.
